text:
sam: quick heads-up: seeing sporadic funcall parse failures on zephyr-int4 canary. payload often looks fine but parser hits trailing garbage.

sam: example raw stream:
```
{"call":"lookup","q":"redwood inference"}

```

nina: any signal on when it happens? batch size, kv cache, seq len?

sam: early look: >75% of failures have batch_size >= 12 and kv_cache enabled. single-request runs almost clean.

raj: sounds like post-quant decode emitting stray bytes. two paths: short-term postproc (sanitize / sentinel) vs long-term runtime fix.

oscar: proposal for canary experiment (all behind flags):
A) baseline
B) sanitizer: strip trailing non-utf8, attempt ndjson-last-object parse, + single retry
C) sentinel-suffix: append `<<SENT:crc32:BASE64>>` after expected funcall output and validate before parse

nina: +1. metrics to collect: schema_compliance, parse_retry_rate, p95/p99 latency, sanitizer_trims_pct, sentinel_collision_count. run 2k samples per arm.

sam: added tiny harness to reproduce with deterministic seeds (pumps batches through quant decode). attached in ticket INF-9777.

canary-bot: zephyr-int4 canary 5% traffic. rolling schema_fail: 3.7% (30m).

raj: implementation notes: make sentinel per-request with 12-byte random salt to avoid collisions. add metric tag `postproc.arm` and `kvcache_hit` to correlate.

oscar: also add parse_error_class metric: invalid_utf8 | trailing_bytes | parse_partial. helps decide sanitizer behavior.

nina: if sanitizer wins but costs latency, we can gate it behind a retry-only flag to avoid p95 regressions.

sam: I'll run the 2k/arm run overnight and post results here. filing follow-ups with runtime team to trace quant->token boundary.

oscar: long-term we should root-cause; postproc is a bandaid. open INF-9778 to instrument raw token bytes on failures.

nina: thanks — ping me when results land.
